question: ________ reduce (s) the size of large fat globules, allowing enzymes to work more effectively.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bile salts**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bile salts** reduce the size of large fat globules, allowing enzymes to work more effectively.
 
• Bile salts are a component of bile, which is produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder.
 
• They play a crucial role in the digestion and absorption of fats in the small intestine.
 
• By emulsifying fats, bile salts increase the surface area available for enzyme action, particularly for the enzyme lipase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrochloric acid** is secreted by the stomach and helps in the digestion of proteins but does not emulsify fats.
 
• **Pancreatic juice** contains enzymes that digest carbohydrates, proteins, and fats but does not emulsify fats.
 
• **Succus entericus** is the intestinal juice that contains various digestive enzymes but does not emulsify fats.
 
• Emulsification of fats is essential for the efficient digestion and absorption of dietary fats.
